purpose: Renders a model's Markdown as it streams in (AI Elements Response / Streamdown), safely. The content is parsed by a small Markdown parser into a tree and rendered with Vue elements — never `v-html` — so raw HTML in model output shows as text, `javascript:`, `data:` and protocol-relative links are dropped (only `http(s)`, `mailto`, `tel`, relative and `#` links survive, checked by the shared `safeHref`), and images render as their alt text. It covers what responses use: paragraphs, headings, bold, italic, inline code, links, lists (nested by indenting an item's lines under it, to any depth), block quotes, GFM tables, rules and fenced code (rendered with `CodeBlock`, copyable). Incomplete Markdown is tolerated while streaming: an unclosed `**` renders bold to the end, an unclosed code fence stays a plain `<pre>` until it closes (no highlighting churn), and a half-written link shows its text only. Text renders at the reading size (`.text-body-lg`) with a full step (`--spacing-md`) between blocks, the plain, wide answer column of a chat. Headings are bold, with an extra `--spacing-sm` above them so a section reads as a new start: `#` at `.text-heading-md`, every deeper level at the reading size. A fenced code block is a filled `CodeBlock` card with the language and copy in a sticky header, the same while the fence is still open. Numbered citations become `Citation` chips resolved against `sources`: `[1]` one chip with the site's mark and name, and a run of markers (`[1][2]`, `[1] [2]`, `[1, 2]`) one chip with `+1` whose card pages through both sources. A blinking caret marks the end while `streaming`; the region is `aria-busy` until the stream ends.
useWhen: Use StreamingResponse for model Markdown that arrives while it renders; a whole documentation page written in MDX uses DocMarkdown.
Any generated text on a page (an explanation, a summary) that arrives token by token.
avoidWhen: Trusted HTML from your own CMS → render it with your CMS pipeline; this component deliberately renders no HTML.
related: `citation`, `sources` — inline references and the panel that lists every source.
`response-loading` — the loading text before the first token, or a bar where a table is coming.
bestPractices: Pass the accumulated text on every chunk; the parser is cheap and the output is keyed by block.
Keep `streaming` true until the stream closes, then false (removes the caret, highlights an open fence).
Pass the response and its `Sources` the same array, so `[n]` is item `n` in both.
Do not post-process model output into HTML; there is no HTML path.
